raw_response:
I will still plant the full 10.1 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation. I do not like changing too much in one year. Around Quzhou, if wheat and maize both want steady yield, I have to feed the wheat a bit heavier, then let the maize eat some of the leftover phosphorus and potassium from the wheat season. I have well water, so I will not wait for the sky if the field is short of moisture at the key time. Fertilizer is real money, but cutting too hard is more dangerous than spending a bit extra. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put enough base fertilizer, then topdress around jointing, and water about three times if the season is normal. For maize, I will use a hybrid, sow right after wheat, mostly no-tillage to save time, use one-shot fertilizer with a little zinc, and give two irrigations if rain is not enough, mainly around jointing and tasseling-grain filling. I will not chase the very highest demo-field yield, but I will aim for a solid crop I can actually bring home on 10.1 mu.
